scope: Collector refusal persistence across loop iterations and restart
Recovery ordering and source digest binding
Incomplete restore rejection by collector and monitor
Compatibility with separately owned backup helper imports and tests

findings.title: Service heartbeat erased a durable collector refusal
findings.root_cause: The service wrote ALIVE_READONLY or NETWORK_DISABLED unconditionally on every wait; health accepted that heartbeat without reading failure events.
findings.reproduction: A synthetic RuntimeError produced REFUSED_COLLECTOR_ERROR; the next service wait wrote ALIVE_READONLY. A later neutral event plus fresh NETWORK_DISABLED heartbeat also returned healthy.
findings.fix: Read bounded validated immutable events for every heartbeat and health check; preserve refusal through neutral events and restart. Clear only for a strictly later successful event bound to existing source bytes by SHA-256. Failure wins equal-second ordering. Monitor reports COLLECTOR_FAIL_CLOSED and exit 2.

findings.title: Incomplete restore marker did not block collector or monitor
findings.root_cause: Trust-root validation checked directories but did not inspect the recovery helper's .restore-incomplete marker.
findings.reproduction: With the marker present, run_once reached the injected fetcher and monitor status accepted the volume.
findings.fix: Reject a present marker, including dangling symlink, in collection, dry-run, heartbeat writing/health, and monitoring. Never clear the marker.
findings.backup_integration_note: Release owner notified to guard _inventory before snapshot staging, because staging only forward/events can otherwise discard the marker. Backup helper changes are outside this patch's ownership.

verification.command: PYTHONPATH=src:. python -m unittest tests.test_strat01_independent_collector tests.test_strat01_local_monitor tests.test_strat01_collector_backup

remaining_limits: Root task owns full-suite and real container integration verification; this review ran only the focused suites.
Event history fails closed beyond 10000 records or 32000 bytes per event.
Heartbeat validation is not a complete source archive audit; monitor retains the complete source audit.
Source SHA-256 binding does not detect coordinated rewriting of both source and event by an actor with filesystem write access.
Existing stale-lock manual review and process signal handling were not changed.
No server deployment, market-data reliability, execution, profitability, or paper-day qualification was tested.
